text:
nita (eng-platform): Heads up — saw a couple of rows from org-558 show up in org-112's dashboard right after the canary flip at ~10:12 PDT. Not huge but reproducible with fast switches.

marco (eng-platform): I noticed something like that earlier on canary-2, thought it was noise. Good catch.

aisling (eng-infra): Any logs or a repro? header vs cookie mismatch?

nita (eng-platform): Quick repro steps I used:
1) Sign in as a user in org-112
2) Quick switch to org-558
3) Switch back to org-112 quickly
Observed: a panel shows 1-2 rows that belong to org-558. Happens ~3/10 tries.

marco (eng-platform): Telemetry shows a pair of backend calls for the panel where the first request went to backend-a and the next to backend-b but the prefetch cache was populated with org-558 data. Suspect route-affinity header sticky on fallback.

aisling (eng-infra): Pulled gateway logs. Found requests where x-org-id=112 but Cookie: active_org=558. Gateway forwarded x-org-id, backend prefetch used cookie precedence and populated cache for the wrong org.

nita (eng-platform): Example request we logged:
```
GET /console/panel?id=33 HTTP/1.1
Host: console.redwood.dev
x-org-id: 112
Cookie: active_org=558; session=abc123
```
Response used prefetch data keyed by cookie org.

marco (eng-platform): So the root cause is handler ordering: routing uses header, prefetch logic uses cookie. Race when user flips org quickly -> mixed signals.

dave (eng-sre): Quick mitigation idea: make prefetch prefer x-org-id header when present. Safer than relying on cookie in our multi-header world.

aisling (eng-infra): I can push a small handler reorder to canary-2: prefer external header over cookie for org resolution. Will draft a tiny patch.

nita (eng-platform): Can you patch canary-2 first and let us hammer it? :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy started for canary-2 (build 5123) by aisling — ETA ~90s

marco (eng-platform): I'll set a temporary alert: cross_org_panel_rows >= 1 on canary-2 to catch regressions.

nita (eng-platform): Ran 20 rapid-switch attempts after the patch — no repro. Looks good.

dave (eng-sre): Follow-up action: add e2e test covering quick-switch header/cookie precedence and a short runbook for incident response.

marco (eng-platform): Filed INF-9876 with details and runbook link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9876

nita (eng-platform): Will add a short note to the postmortem if this pops up again. Thanks all.
